title: Board Advisory: Medication Delivery and Shipping (best practice recommendations)
rule_summary: The Board of Registration in Pharmacy Advisory: Medication Delivery and Shipping (adopted 6/28/18; revised 1/9/25) sets out best practice recommendations that the Board urges all pharmacies to review as a high priority and to consider implementing as appropriate. Its general recommendations are to ensure compliance with federal and state law, including licensure in other states if required; obtain patient consent for delivery or shipping; document the workflow, including verifying the delivery address and product packaging; permit only trained pharmacy personnel to package medications and produce delivery labels; recommend that two employees witness the packaging of controlled substances and maintain documentation; use proper packaging systems, including appropriate containers and tamper resistant tape; and develop quality assurance methods for packaging. For Schedule II-V controlled substances it recommends requiring a signature upon delivery, recording the tracking number, including the pharmacy's address but not its name on the label, and reviewing the Prescription Monitoring Program dispenser guide and M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 18. For temperature-sensitive products it recommends policies for excursions during delivery, a time-test study at least twice yearly (summer and winter), and packing with a barrier layer between cold packs and the medication and a calibrated temperature monitoring device next to the medication. It also addresses hazardous products, delivery to alternative locations (including that a specialty pharmacy delivering to a retail pharmacy for patient pick-up may do so only if delivering the final packaged product, which the receiving pharmacy may not alter), counseling materials, unclaimed products, packages lost in transit (including reporting lost packages containing federally controlled substances or other drugs with abuse potential to the Board in accordance with its Loss or Theft of Controlled Substances policy), and contracted drivers (including a policy that deliveries are not left at the front desk of an assisted living facility or in the hands of a staff member).
exam_relevance: Tests recognition that the delivery and shipping advisory is Board guidance framed as recommendations, layered on the binding sentences of 247 CMR 9.02.

common_confusions: The advisory's items are recommendations the Board urges pharmacies to consider; they are not regulation.
The advisory recommends putting the pharmacy's address but not its name on the label of a Schedule II-V shipment.
verification_notes: Read in full on 2026-09-17 in the advisory PDF linked under Advisories on the Board's Pharmacy Practice Resources page on mass.gov; the page lists it as the current version.
